# Resident-storage access inventory

**Generated by `scripts/storage-access-inventory.py` — do not edit by hand.**
Regenerate after changing `crates/bicdb-core/src/db.rs`; `--check` fails CI when this file is stale.

Phase 0 of [`server-paged-storage-todo.md`](server-paged-storage-todo.md) requires an inventory of every direct access to the resident record state, grouped by operation. This is that inventory.

## Why this number matters

There are **39 direct access sites** across **29 functions**, all reaching the per-collection shards through one of `.shard`, `.shard_by_rowid`, `.shard_mut`, `.shards_mut`, `.read_all()`, `.write_all()`.

This is the set of call sites a second storage engine has to satisfy. It is the gate on Phase 2: until these are expressed against a trait that both an in-memory and a page-backed implementation can provide, disk-resident rows cannot land incrementally — every partial step would leave the tree uncompilable, so the work would arrive as a single unreviewable branch.

The encouraging finding is that `CollectionState` already funnels every access through a small number of accessors rather than exposing `shards` directly. The refactor is mechanical rather than architectural — but it is 95 sites of mechanical, which is a real piece of work and should be scheduled as one.

## Groups

| Group | Functions | Sites |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| point read | 7 | 7 |
| range cursor | 2 | 3 |
| snapshot read | 5 | 5 |
| write | 3 | 6 |
| validation | 5 | 6 |
| maintenance | 4 | 7 |
| recovery | 3 | 5 |
| **total** | **29** | **39** |

Compaction, checkpointing, index and vector rebuilds, statistics, key rotation. Phase 3 replaces whole-database compaction here with bounded, resumable page-level work.

## Index-store access (tracked separately)

A further **6 sites** shard an *ordered index* rather than the record state. They are listed apart from the groups above because conflating them would misstate the size of the Phase 2 refactor, and because they are already behind the swappable `OrderedIndexStore` trait — which is why Phase 4 (persistent secondary indexes) is the cheapest phase relative to its value: the seam it needs already exists, complete with a `ShadowIndexStore` for validating a new implementation against the proven `BTreeMap` one.

- `ShardedBTreeIndexStore` — 6 sites in `collect_exact`, `has_other_id`, `ids_at`, `insert`, `insert_if_unique`, `remove`
